What is DriveLink?

DriveLink is developing a decentralized, ultra-low latency (under 50ms) Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication standard for Automotive AI. It creates a universal speaking layer that lets vehicles broadcast trajectory predictions and intent in real time to prevent collisions and coordinate maneuvers.

What is V2V communication in DriveLink?

In DriveLink, V2V (Vehicle-to-Vehicle) communication is an intent-first protocol operating under 50ms. Rather than merely sensing nearby obstacles via onboard radar or camera, vehicles directly broadcast their planned paths, speed, and braking intent to surrounding vehicles.

How does DriveLink prevent collisions?

DriveLink enables cooperative collision prevention: vehicles broadcast micro-telemetry and trajectory paths over peer-to-peer mesh radio. If a lead vehicle brakes hard or detects a road hazard, trailing vehicles receive the intent packet in under 50ms—triggering instant alerts or automated reaction.

What is the DriveLink ecosystem?

The DriveLink ecosystem consists of four unified layers: drv-mesh (peer-to-peer V2V intent broadcast), drv-infra (V2I municipal smart signals & roadside nodes), Mobile HUD (driver visualizer), and Cloud Fleet Command (macro telemetry & fleet analytics).

What is drv-mesh?

drv-mesh is DriveLink's core peer-to-peer V2V communication layer. It creates an ad-hoc decentralized mesh network directly between vehicles for sub-50ms trajectory prediction and cooperative awareness without relying on cellular towers.

What is drv-infra?

drv-infra connects vehicles to roadside infrastructure (V2I). It interfaces with municipal smart traffic signals, pedestrian beacons, and roadside nodes to optimize traffic corridors and preempt blind-intersection collisions.
